Ruling: equivalent; project retained. The section 179 deduction for a 2025 vehicle, capped at line 9 for a passenger automobile, zero otherwise, on both sides; nested against merged guards.

Ruling: owner's ruling; project retained. The business-use percentage is business miles over total miles to six decimal places, half-up (owner ruling 3c; amb.2025 register); the second rounds the ratio to four places, its own reading of an open point it noted.

Ruling: ambiguity (owner ruling amb.2025.vehicle_business_pct); project retained. The business-use percentage differs in precision: the second rounds business miles over total miles to 4 places; the project uses 6 places, half-up, the owner's ruling amb.2025.vehicle_business_pct on i4562 p. 14, Column (c) ('dividing the number of miles the vehicle is driven for trade or business purposes ... by the total number of miles the vehicle is driven for all purposes'; no precision is given). The second's divisor, the larger of 1 and the total miles, differs from the project's total only when no miles are entered, a vehicle on actual expenses the project refuses (scveh.no_miles). Otherwise the same: the cost times the business-use percentage.

Ruling: ambiguity (owner ruling amb.2025.vehicle_business_pct); project retained. The business-use percentage differs in precision: the second rounds business miles over total miles to 4 places, guarded by larger_of(1, total miles); the project uses 6 places, half-up, the owner's ruling amb.2025.vehicle_business_pct on i4562 p. 14, Column (c) ('dividing the number of miles the vehicle is driven for trade or business purposes ... by the total number of miles the vehicle is driven for all purposes'; no precision is given). Otherwise the same: the cost times the business-use percentage.

Ruling: equivalent within scope; project retained. The special allowance for 2025 vehicles: 100% when acquired after January 19, 2025 and the full allowance is chosen, 40% when acquired earlier or by election, none when elected out, on both sides, with the guards arranged differently; the second's zero for use of 50% or less is a case the project refuses (scveh low_use).

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. For a 2025 vehicle, 100% of line 15 when acquired after January 19, 2025 and the full allowance is chosen, 40% when acquired earlier or when the 40% allowance is elected, zero when elected out, on both sides, with the guards arranged differently (the bonus_choice enumeration is exactly full, forty, none, params/2025.yaml); zero for an earlier vehicle on both sides.

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. Line 18 times the rate chosen by the same convention and recovery-year tests: for 2025 the half-year or mid-quarter rate by the same mid-quarter test, for 2020 to 2024 the rate of the prior convention at the 2025 recovery year, and zero for a 2019 vehicle, the worksheet not being used after the recovery period (Pub. 946 p. 61; BUG-0059), the vehicle's depreciation being figured from the unrecovered basis on both sides. The second spells out the recovery year by placed-in-service year where the project reads the recovery_year table, and names its rate table differently.

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. Line 18 times the rate chosen by the same convention and recovery-year tests; the second chooses the rate and multiplies once, the project chooses between products, the same value in every branch.

Ruling: model error; project retained. For a vehicle placed in service in 2019 the second applies the year 6 rate of the 5-year table; 2025 is that vehicle's seventh recovery year, after the recovery period, when the deduction is the unrecovered basis (p946 p. 61, Deductions After the Recovery Period: 'you can deduct that unrecovered basis after the recovery period ends'), and the 5-year tables have six years (tables/2025/macrs_gds.yaml, y5 hy and mq rows end at year 6). The project enters zero (scveh.line19_earlier). Evaluated: fixture stage14.veh.2019_post (line 18 $60,000, half-year) gives line 19 $0 in the project; the second would enter $3,456 (5.76%). The 2025 and 2020 to 2024 branches are the same (the quarter mapping equals the quarter_convention table).

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. Line 18 times the rate chosen by the same convention and recovery-year tests; the second chooses the rate and multiplies once, the project chooses between products. For a 2019 vehicle the project enters zero, the worksheet not being used after the recovery period (BUG-0059; Pub. 946 p. 61), where the second's rate has no table row; the vehicle's depreciation is figured from the unrecovered basis on both sides.

Ruling: equivalent; project retained. Line 18 times the rate chosen by the same convention and recovery-year tests; the second chooses the rate and multiplies once, the project chooses between products, the same value in every branch.

Ruling: representation; project retained. For a passenger automobile both take the smaller of lines 17 and 19. Vehicles that are not passenger automobiles are not subject to the worksheet's limits (Pub. 946 pp. 61–62, Depreciation Worksheet for Passenger Automobiles): their depreciation and special allowance take line 19 and line 16 directly (scveh.macrs_heavy, scveh.bonus_o), so the worksheet line shown for them is not used.

Ruling: owner's ruling; project retained. The business-use percentage is business miles over total miles to six decimal places, half-up (owner ruling 3c; amb.2025 register); the second rounds the ratio to four places, its own reading of an open point it noted. Otherwise the same.

Ruling: ambiguity (owner ruling amb.2025.vehicle_business_pct); project retained. The business-use percentage differs in precision: the second rounds business miles over total miles to 4 places; the project uses 6 places, half-up, the owner's ruling amb.2025.vehicle_business_pct on i4562 p. 14, Column (c) ('dividing the number of miles the vehicle is driven for trade or business purposes ... by the total number of miles the vehicle is driven for all purposes'; no precision is given). The second's divisor, the larger of 1 and the total miles, differs from the project's total only when no miles are entered, a vehicle on actual expenses the project refuses (scveh.no_miles). The lease inclusion amount the second leaves uncomputed (i1040sc p. 8, Lines 20a and 20b, 'you may have to reduce your deduction by the inclusion amount') is refused in the project by the business screen sc.special ('an inclusion amount for leased property').

Ruling: ambiguity (owner ruling amb.2025.vehicle_business_pct); project retained. The business-use percentage differs in precision: the second rounds business miles over total miles to 4 places, guarded by larger_of(1, total miles); the project uses 6 places, half-up, the owner's ruling amb.2025.vehicle_business_pct on i4562 p. 14, Column (c) ('dividing the number of miles the vehicle is driven for trade or business purposes ... by the total number of miles the vehicle is driven for all purposes'; no precision is given). Example: 2,000 business miles of 3,000 with $6,000 of lease payments gives $4,000.00 in the project (evaluated) and $4,000.20 under the second. The lease inclusion amount the second leaves uncomputed (i1040sc p. 8, Lines 20a and 20b, 'you may have to reduce your deduction by the inclusion amount') is refused in the project by the business screen sc.special ('an inclusion amount for leased property').

Ruling: representation; project retained. For a 2025 vehicle the first-year limit with or without the special allowance, and for an earlier vehicle the limit for its recovery year, on both sides (i4562 Limits for passenger automobiles; Pub. 946 p. 59); the second names its own tables and merges the guards.

Ruling: representation; project retained. The same limits from the same Pub. 946 table (i4562 Table 2): for a 2025 vehicle $20,200 with the special allowance and $12,200 without (the second's note; the project's auto_limit and auto_limit_first_nobonus), and for earlier vehicles the limit of their 2025 recovery year. The second splits the table by allowance (p946.auto_limit_bonus, p946.auto_limit) and keys 2019 and 2020 vehicles at year 6 where the project keys 2019 at year 7; tables/2025/auto_limit.yaml gives the same $5,760 for 2019 at years 6 and 7.

Ruling: representation; project retained. The 2019 vehicle's first year after the recovery period follows the Pub. 946 automobile worksheet on both sides (pp. 61–62): year one the lesser of the limit and the section 179 deduction plus the MACRS amount, years 2 to 6 the lesser of each limit and the table amount, the unrecovered basis cost less their total, and 2025 the lesser of the later-years limit and that, times business use. The second names its own tables and key constants and reads line 7 where the project reads the same later-years limit; its ratio is at four places where the owner ruled six (3c).

Ruling: ambiguity (owner ruling amb.2025.vehicle_business_pct); project retained. The business-use percentage differs in precision: the second rounds business miles over total miles to 4 places, guarded by larger_of(1, total miles); the project uses 6 places, half-up, the owner's ruling amb.2025.vehicle_business_pct on i4562 p. 14, Column (c) ('dividing the number of miles the vehicle is driven for trade or business purposes ... by the total number of miles the vehicle is driven for all purposes'; no precision is given). The other differences are value-neutral: for a passenger automobile placed in service in 2019, after its recovery period, the second keys the year's limit at year 6 where the project keys it at the recovery year, 7, and tables/2025/auto_limit.yaml gives $5,760 for both ('4th & later' repeated); the second takes the first-year amount from its table at year 1 without the special allowance (its line 7 note), which is the project's auto_limit_first_nobonus ($10,100 for 2019; a 2019 vehicle that took the allowance is refused by scveh.screen); and it sums the years in another order.

Ruling: ambiguity (owner ruling amb.2025.vehicle_business_pct); project retained. The business-use percentage differs in precision: the second rounds to 4 places, the project uses 6 places, half-up, the owner's ruling on i4562 p. 14, Column (c) (no precision is given); the second's divisor (the larger of 1 and total miles) differs only with no miles, refused for actual expenses (scveh.no_miles). The other differences are value-neutral: for a vehicle that is not a passenger automobile the second takes line 19, which it sets to zero for a 2019 vehicle as the project's column (h) does; for a passenger automobile placed in service in 2019 it reads line 7 (the limit keyed at year 6) where the project reads auto_limit at the recovery year, 7, and tables/2025/auto_limit.yaml gives $5,760 for both ('4th & later' repeated); it takes the first-year amount from its table at year 1 without the special allowance, which is the project's auto_limit_first_nobonus ($10,100 for 2019; a 2019 vehicle that took the allowance is refused by scveh.screen); and it sums the years in another order.
